sentences.text: 10. Heard learned counsel for the Appellant as well as learned counsel for the State.
Perused the application.

11. Learned counsel for the Appellant at the outset contended that the Appellant, who happens to be the co-accused in T.R. Case No.178 of 2020 has been found guilty of offence punishable under Section 363/109 of IPC by the learned Additional Sessions Judge- cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Nabarangpur vide judgment dated 13.12.2024.

Although the principal accused, namely one Laxmikanta Bisoi has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Section 363,
376(3), 506 of IPC read with 6 POCSO Act and he has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for 20 years, however, so far as the Appellant is concerned, he has been sentenced to undergo RI for three years and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- vide order dated 03.01.2025.

Learned counsel for the Appellant at this juncture contended that the Appellant has been found guilty of abetting the kidnapping of the Victim and, as such, he has been found guilty under Sections 363, 109 of IPC.
He further submitted that in the meantime the Appellant has suffered custodial detention for about 7 to 8 months as he is in custody since 03.01.2025.
12. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand objected to the release of the Appellant on bail on the ground of the gravity and seriousness of the allegation.

13. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the respective parties, on a careful examination of the background facts as well as the impugned judgment, this Court observes that the Appellant has been convicted for commission of crime under Sections 363, 109 of IPC and he has been sentenced to undergo RI for three years.
Taking into consideration the aforesaid facts, this Court is inclined to release the Appellant on bail.
Accordingly, it is directed that the Appellant be released on bail subject to such terms and conditions as deemed just and proper by the trial Court.
14. Accordingly, the I.A. stands allowed.

14. Learned counsel for the Appellant does not want to press this I.A.
15.
Accordingly, the I.A. stands disposed of as not pressed.

( Aditya Kumar Mohapatra ) Judge S.K. Rout Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Page 3 of 3.
